incident-bot: PAGER — euc2-ingress: sudden 5xx/connreset spike detected (>=25% 502s in last 3m). Paging euc2 oncall: @Priya Shah. Incident channel opened.

Priya Shah: I'm oncall, looking. Notified SRE and netops. any early customer hits?

Jess Romero: Support is seeing a handful of errors — ~12 customer reports across EU hosts, mostly API/generation requests timing out then 502. Raising customer-impact.

Tom Nguyen: pulling metrics now — grafana (ingress/euc2) shows a sharp bump starting at 12:04 UTC; 502s and upstream resets. Checking ALB -> envoy -> pod-level.

Aisha Patel: quick ask — can someone check ALB target health and NLB metrics? I want to rule out target group oscillation vs envoy conn exhaustion.

Connor Li: checking Route53 and regional DNS. I see increased latency resolving ingress.euc.redwood.com -> some clients resolving to older NLB IPs in euc2 while ALBs are healthy. Might be a small DNS divergence, TTL is 60s though.

Tom Nguyen: grabbing logs from envoy pod (ingress-controller-7f6b9):
```
[2026-03-15T12:05:11Z] envoy [warning] upstream reset: connection reset by peer, upstream 10.0.23.45:8080
[2026-03-15T12:05:12Z] envoy [error] downstream stream reset: connection termination
[2026-03-15T12:05:13Z] http 502 /v1/generate -> upstream reset (exceeded retries)
```
Restart count on one ingress pod is high: `kubectl -n ingress get pods` shows ingress-controller-7f6b9 (RESTARTS 18).

Priya Shah: that restart count looks like a leak. Before rolling anything, can we shift some traffic off euc2 to buy time? Connor, can you do a quick weighted DNS change or Route53 failover?

Connor Li: I can do a weighted change. Preparing a Route53 change-batch to move 40% traffic to euc1 for the ingress CNAME. Will apply now and monitor. CMD: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://shift-euc2-to-euc1.json` (change sets prepared). Applying in 10s.

EdgeBot: deploy-bot: DNS change submitted (change id: /change/CMS123456). TTL respected ~60s.

Priya Shah: thanks. Meanwhile Tom, what's the risk of a rolling restart of the ingress controllers? We have enough capacity in euc2 if we do one-by-one.

Tom Nguyen: risk acceptable — rolling restart will drop some in-flight KV caches but we have prefix caching elsewhere. Plan: `kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller` and watch 1 pod at a time (maxUnavailable 1). I'll run it and watch error rate.

Tom Nguyen: executing restart now.

Aisha Patel: I'm also bumping envoy keepalive and conntrack in the config map (increase keepalive_timeout from 10s -> 30s) to reduce upstream resets. Patching now.

Tom Nguyen: first ingress pod restarted, health checks re-registered. 502s falling from 28% -> 12% after first pod came back. Rolling through others.

Connor Li: Route53 metrics show the weighted shift in place; client-side resolution trending to euc1. We should see aggregated errors drop as traffic migrates.

Priya Shah: Jess — customer comms? Severity?

Jess Romero: marking sev2. Customers with errors are experiencing degraded response / retries; recommend a short banner on status page noting degraded requests in EU while we mitigate. I'll draft copy: "We are investigating elevated 5xx error rates impacting some EU customers. Mitigation in progress."

EdgeBot: incident-bot: automated notes saved to timeline. Severity set to SEV2 by oncall.

Tom Nguyen: after full restart + keepalive patch, 502 rate back to baseline ~2.3% in 6m window. Upstream reset logs decreased significantly. Connection reset rate reduced by ~85%.

Priya Shah: Connor — keep the weighted DNS shift for 30m to ensure cache clears. We'll revert after confirming stability. Also file a ticket to sweep client-resolve discrepancies (why some clients kept hitting stale NLB IPs).

Connor Li: ack — keeping 40%->euc1 for 30m, will revert via change-batch. Investigating why some resolvers cached older records beyond TTL (seen in AS/edge-level).

Aisha Patel: follow-up: create a small change to healthcheck threshold and backoff so unhealthy targets don't trigger rapid restarts. Also schedule an Envoy version bump test — suspect a connection leak in current envoy build under high NLB churn.

Tom Nguyen: collecting pod profiles and envoy admin dump for postmortem: `curl localhost:9901/stats?filter=cluster_manager.*reset` — saved to s3://redwood-incidents/2412001234/

Priya Shah: Handoff: I'll remain the coordinator for next 30m, then hand to Tom for follow-up and RCA. Postmortem required with timeline, root cause hypothesis (envoy conn leak + DNS resolution divergence), and remediation (fix envoy, improve DNS routing, add guard rails).

Jess Romero: status page updated and customer follow-ups queued. I'll notify account teams for affected customers.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) — 502s returned to normal baseline after restarts and DNS shift. Closing pager.

Priya Shah: Thanks team. Please append any logs, commands, and notes to the incident timeline and create the postmortem ticket (INC-241200). I'll tag SRE, NetOps, and Eng-Platform for RCA. :thumbsup:
